sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2025
sources.supports: A web-app baseline covering access control, configuration, supply chain, crypto, injection, design, authentication, integrity, logging, and exceptional-condition handling.
sources.limits: An awareness taxonomy, not a project-specific checklist or proof that a control works.

sources.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
sources.supports: A versioned catalogue of web-application verification requirements; its levels are assurance-depth selections for scoping verification, not a generic ranking of product risk.
sources.limits: The landing page confirmed 5.0.0 but did not expose the detailed level definitions in the fetched extract; cite the version with individual requirements before prescribing a level. Owner resolved level wording using pinned source S26.

sources.title: OWASP API Security Top 10
sources.supports: API checks for object and function authorization, authentication, resource consumption, sensitive business flows, SSRF, configuration, inventory, and third-party API use.
sources.limits: API-focused guidance; it does not replace web, mobile, or cloud configuration guidance.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and Generative AI
sources.supports: AI-feature modules for prompt injection, sensitive-data disclosure, supply chain, poisoning, output handling, agency, prompt leakage, vector/embedding isolation, misinformation, and bounded consumption.
sources.limits: A risk catalogue; each application still needs code-enforced authorization, validation, and product-specific abuse controls.

sources.title: OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard
sources.supports: Mobile modules for storage, cryptography, authentication/authorization, network communication, platform interaction, code quality, resilience, and privacy.
sources.limits: The fetched page did not display a release number; do not label it with an inferred version. Release number resolved by S24: 2.1.0.

sources.title: OWASP Mobile Application Security Testing Guide
sources.supports: Mobile testing references aligned to the MAS project, useful when a repository contains a native mobile app.
sources.limits: The fetched page did not display a release number; it is testing guidance and does not establish compliance by itself. Release number resolved by S25: 2.0.0.

sources.title: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Authentication flows: generic failure handling, automated-attack resistance, MFA, and event monitoring.
sources.limits: Choose controls and thresholds for the product; the page is not a turnkey authentication design.

sources.title: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Session-cookie and lifecycle checks when an app uses browser sessions.
sources.limits: Applies differently to token-based native and service-to-service clients.

sources.title: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Password-hash storage checks for applications that own password verification.
sources.limits: Does not apply when an external identity provider alone owns passwords.

sources.title: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Boundary validation and allow-list-oriented handling for untrusted request data.
sources.limits: Validation complements output encoding and authorization; it is not a substitute for either.

sources.title: OWASP Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: CSRF protections for state-changing browser requests authenticated by cookies.
sources.limits: Usually not applicable to non-browser or bearer-token-only flows; confirm the client/auth model.

sources.title: OWASP Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Controls for server-side URL fetching, including allowlisting and network-boundary safeguards.
sources.limits: Only applies when the service follows user- or content-influenced URLs; DNS and redirect behavior need stack-specific handling.

sources.title: OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Upload controls such as allowed formats, size bounds, storage separation, and handling of untrusted files.
sources.limits: Applies only to upload or import features; malware scanning and retention are deployment choices.

sources.title: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Secret lifecycle, access, rotation, and non-disclosure practices for source and runtime configuration.
sources.limits: A local source scan can detect patterns but cannot prove a credential is valid or safely rotated.

sources.title: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Security-event logging and safe treatment of sensitive or untrusted log data.
sources.limits: Logging policy is not monitoring coverage; operational retention and alerting require environment-specific setup.

sources.title: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: HTTPS, endpoint-local access control, and token/API design checks for REST services.
sources.limits: Designed for REST-style APIs; do not use it as the sole reference for GraphQL or browser pages.

sources.title: OWASP GraphQL Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: GraphQL validation, authorization, query-cost, batching, and introspection-aware review.
sources.limits: Applies only when GraphQL is present; schema and resolver behavior still need local inspection.

sources.title: OWASP Node.js Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Node-specific application, error, server, and platform hardening pointers.
sources.limits: Framework and hosting defaults vary; validate against the actual Node stack.

sources.title: OWASP Django Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Django checks including production debug state, built-in authentication protections, dependency upkeep, and throttling options.
sources.limits: Django defaults can be overridden; inspect settings and deployment configuration locally.

sources.title: OWASP Docker Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Container checks such as timely updates, avoiding Docker-socket exposure, and running as an unprivileged user.
sources.limits: Container image review does not assess the host or orchestrator configuration.

sources.title: OWASP Kubernetes Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Cluster host, component, build, deployment, and runtime security coverage.
sources.limits: Use only where Kubernetes manifests or a cluster target exist; local manifests cannot prove managed-cluster posture.

sources.title: OWASP HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Response-header choices, including browser-facing security headers and deployment considerations.
sources.limits: A Content Security Policy needs staged, app-specific validation; headers should be checked against a local response.

sources.title: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
sources.supports: The collection and maintenance context for the topical cheat sheets above.
sources.limits: An index, not a single prescriptive launch standard.

sources.title: OpenSSF Scorecard README and checks
sources.supports: A release checklist can inspect public-repository practices such as workflow risks, branch protection, token permissions, packaging, and signed releases.
sources.limits: Scorecard is an assessment tool and does not replace repository-specific review.

sources.title: SLSA Security levels
sources.supports: Build L1 records provenance, L2 requires hosted signed provenance and consumer validation, and L3 adds hardened build isolation.
sources.limits: SLSA describes supply-chain guarantees; it does not assess application authorization or runtime configuration. Owner confirmed Approved v1.2 in S20; v1.1 is historical, not the current baseline.

sources.title: Concise Guide for Developing More Secure Software
sources.supports: Checklist prompts for MFA on privileged developer accounts, dependency selection and monitoring, tests, secret prevention, review, a security policy, signed releases, SBOMs, and SLSA.
sources.limits: It is broad guidance; individual changes need stack-specific validation.

sources.title: GitHub Actions hardening documentation
sources.supports: No rule recorded: the requested documentation URL returned 404 during this pass.
sources.limits: Use a current GitHub Docs URL before turning this into a normative checklist item. Correct current path was read as S21.

sources.title: OpenSSF Scorecard beginner checks for GitHub workflows
sources.supports: Default workflow token permissions should be restrictive and each action should receive only permissions it needs.
sources.limits: This does not establish a complete GitHub repository-security baseline.

sources.title: npm trusted publishing
sources.supports: npm can use a configured OIDC trusted publisher from supported cloud CI, avoiding long-lived publish tokens; public packages from public repositories can receive automatic provenance.
sources.limits: Only applies to npm publication, and provenance has documented public-repository limitations.

sources.title: PyPI trusted publishers
sources.supports: PyPI can exchange CI OIDC identity for a short-lived, project-scoped publishing token instead of placing a long-lived API token in CI.
sources.limits: Applies only to package publication workflows configured as trusted publishers.

sources.title: Supabase Row Level Security
sources.supports: For every exposed table, pair least-privilege grants with operation-specific RLS policies and allow/deny tests; service-role/secret keys bypass RLS and belong only on the server.
sources.limits: The correct policies depend on the product's authorization model; migration and RLS-policy changes require explicit approval.

sources.title: Firebase Security Rules
sources.supports: Firebase deployments need reviewed service-specific rules rather than relying on default open access.
sources.limits: Fetched page content was navigation-heavy in this pass; consult the service-specific Rules testing documentation before prescribing exact syntax.

sources.title: Vercel security documentation
sources.supports: Conditional hosting review point for Vercel projects.
sources.limits: Fetch completed but extracted body was elided by the tool output; no precise platform configuration rule is recorded.

sources.title: Netlify secure access documentation
sources.supports: Conditional hosting review point for Netlify projects.
sources.limits: Fetch completed but extracted body was elided by the tool output; no precise platform configuration rule is recorded.

sources.title: Cloudflare account security documentation
sources.supports: Conditional hosting review point for Cloudflare projects.
sources.limits: Fetch completed but extracted body was elided by the tool output; no precise platform configuration rule is recorded.

sources.title: AWS shared responsibility model
sources.supports: Conditional AWS review should distinguish AWS-managed infrastructure responsibilities from customer configuration responsibilities.
sources.limits: The shared-responsibility model does not provide resource-specific hardening settings.

sources.title: Amazon S3 Block Public Access
sources.supports: Public-storage exposure is a conditional launch check for S3-backed uploads and assets.
sources.limits: Fetched as primary documentation but no exact configuration assertion is recorded here because the output was elided. Owner added direct official page S31.

sources.title: Stripe webhook signature verification
sources.supports: Verify Stripe-Signature using the endpoint secret and the unchanged UTF-8 request body; body parsers must not alter the webhook body before verification.
sources.limits: This does not by itself define event replay handling or application business logic.

sources.title: Stripe idempotent requests
sources.supports: Conditional payments module should review idempotency for client retries.
sources.limits: Fetched as primary documentation but no exact configuration assertion is recorded here because the output was elided. Owner completed direct reading in S27.

sources.title: Next.js environment variables
sources.supports: `NEXT_PUBLIC_` is a client-exposure marker and must be treated as unsuitable for secrets.
sources.limits: Exact page content was elided in the combined fetch; verify the current framework wording before citation in a public skill. Owner added direct official page S30; no unverified runtime-version claim.

sources.title: Vite environment variables and modes
sources.supports: `VITE_` values are bundled into client source, so they must not contain sensitive values; local env files should be ignored by Git.
sources.limits: The prefix rule is Vite-specific and is not a generic secret-detection rule.

sources.title: Express behind proxies
sources.supports: Rate-limiting and logging should use a client IP derived from a proxy setup that exactly matches deployment; blindly setting `trust proxy` to true can allow client-supplied forwarded headers to control the value.
sources.limits: The proper trust configuration depends on the actual proxy chain and must be tested in that deployment topology.

sources.title: MITRE CWE Top 25
sources.edition: 2025; current landing page lists this year
sources.supports: Prioritization context for recurring software weakness classes.
sources.limits: Population ranking is not an application-specific risk score.

sources.title: NIST Secure Software Development Framework
sources.supports: Lifecycle practices, security requirements, release integrity and vulnerability response.
sources.limits: A framework to tailor, not a certification or automatic checklist.

sources.title: NIST SSDF revision
sources.edition: SP 800-218 Rev. 1 / 1.2; initial public draft, December 17 2025
sources.supports: Identifies the newer draft and prevents presenting it as the final baseline.
sources.limits: Draft status explicit; normative recommendations use S02 until a final successor is verified.

sources.title: NIST Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication
sources.supports: Confirms the current revision and its authentication scope.
sources.limits: Government-system scope; do not claim every commercial app is legally bound by it.

sources.title: NIST authenticator requirements
sources.supports: Password-only minimum is 15 characters; MFA passwords may use 8. Supports blocklists and avoiding composition rules and routine forced changes.
sources.limits: Separate centrally checked passwords from device unlock secrets; changes to existing auth require approval.

sources.title: CISA Secure by Design hub and joint guidance
sources.edition: Current hub unavailable; October 2023 joint paper seen in primary-source index
sources.supports: Source discovery only; an indexed primary extract describes manufacturer responsibility and secure defaults.
sources.limits: Hub returned 403; PDF retrieval failed, and partner PDF exceeded tool size. Do not claim full paper review or newest CISA edition. Use S07/S02 for supported principles.

sources.title: ASD Secure by Design foundations
sources.edition: July 2024 document; HTML last updated July 30 2024
sources.supports: Security defaults and lifecycle ownership as design responsibilities.
sources.limits: Partner-government guidance, not a substitute for inaccessible CISA publication verification.

sources.title: MDN Web Security
sources.supports: Browser-facing controls: HTTPS, safer content handling, cookie restrictions and cross-origin boundaries.
sources.limits: Choose applicable controls; no operational environment or application has been audited.

sources.title: Mozilla HTTP Observatory tests and scoring
sources.supports: Browser-header checks and interpretation of their grades.
sources.limits: Grade is a signal, not proof of authorization, tenant separation or complete security; no remote scan was run.

sources.title: Security disclosure file format
sources.supports: A discoverable security contact with expiry, normally at /.well-known/security.txt over HTTPS.
sources.limits: Use a user-approved real contact; a placeholder contact is not a completed disclosure channel.

sources.title: MDN CSP Report-Only
sources.supports: Trial a policy while observing violations before enforcement.
sources.limits: Report-Only does not block violations. External reporting destinations need separate data-sharing approval.

sources.title: MDN Strict-Transport-Security
sources.supports: HSTS relies on an HTTPS response; subdomain scope and preload require care.
sources.limits: An HTTP localhost header check cannot prove HTTPS enforcement; do not casually add preload or includeSubDomains.

sources.title: MDN CORS
sources.supports: Credentialed browser access needs explicit allowed origins; public noncredentialed resources can allow all origins.
sources.limits: CORS controls browser response access, not caller authorization or all cross-site requests.

sources.title: Electron security guidance
sources.edition: Rolling latest documentation; no app-version claim
sources.supports: Renderer isolation, sandboxing, remote-content and privileged-bridge boundaries.
sources.limits: Only applicable to Electron; another desktop runtime needs its own official guidance.

sources.title: MCP authorization specification
sources.supports: Validate access-token audience and use constrained authorization scopes.
sources.limits: Map controls to the detected transport and SDK version; reading docs does not authorize connector changes.

sources.title: MCP security best practices
sources.supports: Threat discovery: confused deputy, unsafe token forwarding, SSRF and local-server execution.
sources.limits: Draft is supplementary; use S15 for stable normative authorization requirements.

sources.title: Django deployment checklist
sources.supports: Check production debug settings, hosts and environment-specific deployment configuration.
sources.limits: Installed applications may use a different supported version; inspect their manifests first.

sources.title: FastAPI behind a proxy
sources.supports: Forwarded headers should be accepted from known proxy addresses.
sources.limits: Trusting all sources is only appropriate under an enforced proxy-only network boundary; inspect topology.

sources.title: EU General Data Protection Regulation
sources.supports: When applicable, data minimization, retention, security and an appropriate processing basis need attention.
sources.limits: No jurisdiction or lawful-basis determination made. Consent is not the only possible basis; legal decisions stay with the user and qualified advisers.

sources.title: SLSA specification
sources.supports: Current supply-chain framework with build/source tracks and provenance.
sources.limits: Supersedes P02 as this research baseline; provenance alone does not establish safe behavior or a SLSA level.

sources.title: GitHub Actions secure use
sources.supports: Least workflow privilege, handling untrusted event data safely, and full commit-SHA references for third-party actions.
sources.limits: An immutable action can still be unsafe; inspect source and update deliberately. Replaces unavailable P04.

sources.title: GitHub repository-security quickstart
sources.supports: Repository security-policy and security-feature setup pointers.
sources.limits: Plan availability and dashboard state are not verified from local files; user performs remote setup.

sources.title: npm publishing 2FA requirements
sources.supports: Maintainer authentication and package publishing protections.
sources.limits: Account settings and publication remain user actions; recheck supported publishing paths before implementation.

sources.title: MASVS release ledger
sources.supports: Confirms stable mobile baseline including privacy controls.
sources.limits: O05 is live documentation; pin a release for precise requirements. Do not reuse old MASVS level labels uncritically.

sources.title: MASTG release ledger
sources.edition: 2.0.0 marked Latest; first stable v2 framework
sources.supports: Confirms modular mobile test guidance and stable edition.
sources.limits: Use detected platform tools locally; missing device/emulator support must be reported.

sources.title: ASVS usage and verification levels
sources.supports: L1 starts with essential defenses; L2 includes L1 and broader requirements; L3 adds the most demanding controls. Tailoring depends on application context.
sources.limits: A selected subset is ASVS-informed, not an ASVS certification. GitHub latest release alias also exposes bleeding-edge content; do not substitute it for v5.0.0.

sources.title: Stripe idempotent requests
sources.supports: Use an operation-specific key to make supported API retries return the recorded outcome.
sources.limits: API request idempotency is different from deduplicating incoming webhook events; payment edits require separate approval.

sources.title: Supabase API key types
sources.supports: Distinguishes publishable/anon keys from privileged secret/service-role keys that bypass RLS.
sources.limits: Prefix presence is not proof of a leak. Assess privileges and RLS without displaying key values.

sources.title: Firebase basic security rules
sources.supports: Tailor rules to authenticated users and the intended data access model rather than broad public access.
sources.limits: Product-specific rules differ; privileged server SDK paths also need server-side authorization.

sources.title: Next.js environment variables
sources.edition: Rolling App Router guide; selector showed 16.3.6
sources.supports: Investigate NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables as browser-exposure candidates alongside build artifacts.
sources.limits: Prefix is a signal, not proof a value is confidential; use version-specific instructions for the target app.

sources.title: Amazon S3 Block Public Access
sources.supports: Inspect account/bucket public-access controls and deliberate public-object requirements.
sources.limits: Local IaC is only desired state; dashboard and actual resource state remain unverified. No AWS calls made.

sources.title: Vercel Deployment Protection
sources.supports: Conditional review of preview/deployment access boundaries.
sources.limits: Do not assume features are included in a plan or that platform protection replaces app authorization.

sources.title: Cloudflare security guidance
sources.supports: Conditional provider-security documentation entry point.
sources.limits: No account, origin lock-down or plan-specific settings verified; select implementation pages only when Cloudflare is detected.

sources.title: Auth0 production-deployment guidance
sources.supports: Conditional identity-provider pointer only.
sources.limits: Retrieval failed. No Auth0-specific checklist rule is derived; fetch current docs when provider is present.

sources.title: PortSwigger access-control guidance
sources.supports: Use resource-level authorization tests, including role and cross-user boundaries.
sources.limits: Practitioner evidence, corroborated by O03/O16/S26; no lab or attack was executed.

sources.title: Trail of Bits Testing Handbook
sources.supports: Choose deterministic analysis suited to the language and risk.
sources.limits: Tool discovery, not permission to install tools or run arbitrary rule downloads; corroborated by S02.

sources.title: Troy Hunt: Passwords Evolved
sources.supports: Helpful explanation of credential reuse and usable authentication.
sources.limits: Do not inherit old numeric policy; use S04/S05/O09 for current requirements.

sources.title: Tanya Janca: Resources
sources.supports: Accessible teaching style for developers without a security background.
sources.limits: No technical control imported from the landing page. Linked securecodingguideline.com could not be retrieved.

sources.title: Jim Manico: Talks and workshops
sources.supports: Coverage signal for secure coding, frontend boundaries, dependencies and AI/MCP.
sources.limits: Talk descriptions are not standards or verified talk transcripts; checklist authority remains OWASP/NIST.

sources.title: Latacora: Cryptographic right answers
sources.supports: Prefer established cryptographic constructions and proper password hashing.
sources.limits: Use current O09/S05 guidance; do not carry over historical preference ordering or custom crypto recipes.

sources.title: Turnstile server-side validation
sources.supports: A challenge must be validated on the server before its protected action.
sources.limits: Conditional example; no provider purchase or live call authorized.

sources.title: Cloudflare DDoS Protection
sources.supports: An edge service can absorb some network/HTTP abuse before origin handling.
sources.limits: Not a replacement for origin authorization, application budgets or verifying proxy topology.

sources.title: OWASP Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards
sources.supports: Restrict user-controlled redirect destinations.
sources.limits: Validate the actual framework URL parsing and intended redirect flow.

sources.title: Sender Policy Framework
sources.supports: Domain policy identifies permitted sending systems.
sources.limits: RFC 7208 is a referenced standard, not a claim that no updates exist; actual DNS is user-owned.

sources.title: DKIM Signatures
sources.supports: Domain signatures support message authentication.
sources.limits: Private signing keys are not inspected; provider-specific DNS and later amendments must be checked.

sources.title: DMARC
sources.supports: Align domain authentication and publish receiver-handling/reporting policy.
sources.limits: Foundational RFC; check current amendments/provider support before final DNS instructions. Monitoring is not enforcement.

sources.title: Dependabot version updates
sources.supports: Schedule dependency update pull requests for configured ecosystems.
sources.limits: Not automatic safe merging; remote enablement and privileged CI require user action.

local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not reuse its prose, code samples, control lists, or exact decision wording.

local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not reuse its procedures, payloads, commands, or prose.

local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not reuse its benchmark mappings, commands, or prose.

local_skills.useful: Treat retrieved documents and other indirect content as untrusted before model ingestion.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not reuse its pipeline, detector selections, validation criteria, or prose.

local_skills.useful: Defense-in-depth framing for direct and indirect prompt injection.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not reuse its install instructions, detector parameters, code, or prose.

local_skills.useful: MCP-specific focus on untrusted tool metadata, permissions, authentication, SSRF, and change detection.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not reuse its scanner workflow, probes, commands, mappings, or prose.

local_skills.useful: Workflow inventory: unpinned actions, expression-to-shell flow, excess token access, third-party write access, and dependency confusion.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not copy its scripts, examples, threat labels, or scanner workflow.

local_skills.useful: Treat package lifecycle scripts and package acquisition as potentially executable; prefer static inspection and isolation for any malware triage.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not copy its lengthy procedure, commands, examples, or unverified campaign claims.

local_skills.useful: Check internal package naming and registry-source restrictions when a project mixes public and private registries.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not copy its testing tools, implementation instructions, examples, or historical claims.

local_skills.useful: Keep cloud inspection read-only, avoid unsupported conclusions, and summarize sensitive findings.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not copy its service-routing rules or operational API instructions.

local_skills.useful: A cloud module should distinguish a posture review from application testing and require authorized scope.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not copy benchmark mappings, vendor tooling instructions, claims, or remediation timelines.

local_skills.useful: When personal data is in scope, inventory data purposes, retention, processors, and rights as a separate user-owned launch track.
local_skills.do_not_copy: Do not copy legal interpretations, regional claims, templates, calculations, or procedural text.

local_skills.useful: Optional ownership-maintenance context for larger repos.
local_skills.do_not_copy: No mandatory graph analysis, dependency installation or bus-factor claims for a small launch pass.

local_skills.useful: Trust-boundary inventory, conditional checks, evidence and permission distinctions.
local_skills.do_not_copy: No verbatim prose/code, fixed bcrypt cost as universal policy, automatic CSP enforcement, secret-printing grep, blanket wildcard-CORS accusations, universal consent claims, or unsupported statistics.

controls.item: Know what is exposed and what data is held
controls.implementation: Inspect manifests, entry points, CI and data paths without opening secret values.
controls.verification: Cite evidence for each selected profile and module; record unknowns.
controls.why: A short inventory keeps irrelevant advice out of the launch list.

controls.item: Keep confidential values out of shipped files
controls.implementation: Inspect references to credentials; allowlist placeholders and documented public keys.
controls.verification: Redacted local scan plus built-artifact check; no online key validation.
controls.why: Privileged values in public files can grant access immediately.

controls.item: Keep builds repeatable and dependencies understood
controls.implementation: Identify authoritative package manager/lock boundary; inspect scripts before execution.
controls.verification: Locked build/audit where installed and permitted; absent tools stay NOT RUN.
controls.why: Repeatable inputs make updates and advisory findings easier to assess.

controls.item: Choose a clear security contact
controls.implementation: Draft SECURITY.md; add security.txt for a web origin when relevant.
controls.verification: Check usable approved contact and expiry format; no live submission.
controls.why: A working contact lets people report a problem privately.

controls.item: Record what was checked and what remains
controls.implementation: Separate planned action from observed behavior and unavailable environment evidence.
controls.verification: Each claimed pass has command, exit result and bounded evidence.
controls.why: Clear evidence prevents an unchecked setting from looking finished.

controls.item: Serve browser traffic securely
controls.implementation: Review HTTPS termination and scoped HSTS, then provider handoff.
controls.verification: Local TLS/config check only; HTTP localhost cannot prove deployed HSTS.
controls.why: Encrypted transport protects data on its way to the service.

controls.item: Set baseline browser response headers
controls.owner: Agent after plan; ask for enforcement
controls.implementation: Choose content-type, framing and referrer controls that fit the app. CSP rollout is W06, not a required day-one enforcement project.
controls.verification: Inspect local responses and browser console; label Report-Only as monitoring.
controls.why: Browser defaults can be tightened without redesigning the app.

controls.item: Allow only intended cross-origin access
controls.implementation: Separate private credentialed APIs from intentionally public resources.
controls.verification: Allowed and denied origin preflights; normal same-origin flow still works.
controls.why: Only intended browser origins should read private responses.

controls.item: Prevent cross-site state changes
controls.when: Ambient browser credentials and write operations
controls.owner: Agent proposes; ask if session semantics change
controls.implementation: Use framework CSRF controls and appropriate cookie/Origin policy.
controls.verification: Missing/invalid CSRF proof fails; valid same-user request succeeds.
controls.why: A signed-in browser can otherwise submit an unwanted action from another site.

controls.item: Show useful errors without debug internals
controls.implementation: Disable production debug; define safe failure responses.
controls.verification: Local production-mode error exposes no stack/credential data.
controls.why: Debug output may reveal implementation and user data.

controls.item: Protect accounts and administrative actions
controls.implementation: Check server-side authentication plus role/resource authorization.
controls.verification: Signed-out request is denied; ordinary user cannot use admin action.
controls.why: Knowing who signed in is different from checking what they may do.

controls.item: Use appropriate password and recovery controls
controls.implementation: Use current hash/policy guidance and bounded recovery flow; prefer maintained identity components.
controls.verification: Local policy/hash/recovery tests with fake accounts; no real-user resets.
controls.why: Credential storage and recovery are common paths into accounts.

controls.item: Keep sessions scoped and revocable
controls.implementation: Review cookie scope, flags, expiry and rotation without breaking expected login flows.
controls.verification: Inspect synthetic Set-Cookie flags and local logout/expiry behavior.
controls.why: Session scope and expiry limit how long stolen sessions remain useful.

controls.item: Bound login and recovery attempts
controls.implementation: Apply endpoint/account-aware budgets without enabling trivial account lockout.
controls.verification: Bounded valid/invalid request sequence hits limit; unrelated local account can still authenticate.
controls.why: Repeated guesses and reset attempts should have a practical ceiling.

controls.item: Keep tenant and user records separated
controls.owner: Ask if auth, schema or policy changes
controls.implementation: Derive tenant scope from verified identity and enforce on every read/write path.
controls.verification: Two seeded tenants: cross-tenant access denied, same-tenant access succeeds.
controls.why: One customer must not read or change another customer’s records.

controls.item: Protect Supabase tables, views and privileged access
controls.implementation: Review grants/RLS and elevated key paths; avoid broad replacement policies.
controls.verification: Local nonprivileged users cannot cross tenants; privileged bypass paths audited separately.
controls.why: Database policies protect browser-facing data even when a client calls the API directly.

controls.item: Limit Firebase access to the intended users
controls.implementation: Review product-specific rules and server SDK authorization.
controls.verification: Emulator tests deny anonymous and cross-user access while allowing intended access.
controls.why: Broad rules can expose records without going through the app interface.

controls.item: Use the identity provider safely
controls.owner: User dashboard; ask per code item
controls.implementation: Read the actual provider/version docs for redirect, token and session settings.
controls.verification: Local token/redirect mocks; dashboard configuration remains unverified.
controls.why: A managed provider still needs the right application boundaries.

controls.item: Validate input and encode output
controls.owner: Agent after plan; ask if public contract changes
controls.implementation: Use existing schemas, parameterized storage and context-appropriate encoding.
controls.verification: Malformed input denied; stored/displayed untrusted data stays inert.
controls.why: Untrusted values should not become commands, queries or executable markup.

controls.item: Bound work, payloads and waiting time
controls.implementation: Limit body/file size, request duration and concurrency based on actual workloads.
controls.verification: Small bounded local probes verify rejection and timeout without load testing.
controls.why: Small bounded requests should not trigger unlimited work.

controls.item: Trust forwarded addresses only through known proxies
controls.owner: Agent app settings; ask for network/IaC
controls.implementation: Model the allowed hop chain; do not trust arbitrary X-Forwarded-For.
controls.verification: Direct spoofed header cannot evade local limiter; approved proxy path preserves identity.
controls.why: An attacker-supplied address must not become a fresh rate-limit identity.

controls.item: Accept uploads without granting execution
controls.implementation: Bound size/type/path, rename safely, store outside executable/public paths unless deliberate.
controls.verification: Fake files, misleading extensions and traversal names denied; valid fixture accepted.
controls.why: An uploaded file should remain data rather than execute or overwrite files.

controls.item: Keep URL fetches inside their intended destinations
controls.when: URL import, previews, callbacks or discovery
controls.owner: Agent after plan; ask for infra changes
controls.implementation: Restrict scheme/host/address and redirects; account for DNS re-resolution.
controls.verification: Mock resolver/HTTP client rejects private/metadata destinations; no real target probing.
controls.why: A public URL field must not become access to private network services.

controls.item: Keep sensitive records out of logs
controls.implementation: Redact at logging boundaries and retain only useful diagnostic fields.
controls.verification: Synthetic markers absent from captured local logs; no live secrets logged.
controls.why: Diagnostics should remain useful without collecting confidential content.

controls.item: Bound GraphQL and API resource access
controls.owner: Agent after plan; contract changes ask-first
controls.implementation: Review depth/complexity/pagination and field-level authorization as applicable.
controls.verification: Oversized synthetic query denied; authorized bounded query succeeds.
controls.why: A valid query can still request excessive or unauthorized data.

controls.item: Verify incoming payment events
controls.implementation: Use provider SDK raw-body signature validation before side effects.
controls.verification: Local signed fixture accepted; altered body/signature rejected. No Stripe calls.
controls.why: Only authentic provider events should change payment state.

controls.item: Avoid processing the same payment twice
controls.implementation: Separate outgoing idempotency keys from incoming event deduplication.
controls.verification: Repeat local event/request fixture produces one intended effect.
controls.why: Retries should not create duplicate payment effects.

controls.item: Authenticate other incoming webhooks
controls.owner: Agent after plan; new auth scheme ask-first
controls.implementation: Follow the provider signature/replay contract and validate payloads.
controls.verification: Forged and replayed local messages denied; valid message succeeds.
controls.why: External events need a verifiable sender and bounded processing.

controls.item: Make storage exposure deliberate
controls.owner: User dashboard; ask per IaC item
controls.implementation: Separate intended public assets from private objects, policies and signed access.
controls.verification: Local config/policy tests; actual bucket state remains user-owned/unverified.
controls.why: Private files should stay private even when their URLs are guessed.

controls.item: Protect preview and management surfaces
controls.implementation: Select Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare/AWS controls only for the detected host.
controls.verification: Read config evidence and provide exact user verification steps; no remote probes.
controls.why: Preview and management surfaces may expose unfinished or internal functions.

controls.item: Give containers only needed privileges
controls.implementation: Review user, capabilities, mounts, secret handling and image provenance.
controls.verification: Static config checks and approved local container checks; no production access.
controls.why: A container compromise should have as little reach as possible.

controls.item: Keep Kubernetes identities and workloads scoped
controls.owner: Ask per IaC item; user applies
controls.implementation: Review RBAC, pod privilege, network boundaries and secret references.
controls.verification: Offline manifest checks; no cluster remediation or live scanning.
controls.why: Cluster-wide permissions can turn a small workload issue into a larger one.

controls.item: Keep model credentials on the server
controls.owner: Agent code after plan; user rotates
controls.implementation: Remove privileged model keys from client build paths; protect the server endpoint.
controls.verification: Fresh client build contains no synthetic secret marker; no paid model call.
controls.why: A browser bundle cannot keep a model-provider secret confidential.

controls.item: Put a ceiling on AI spending and loops
controls.implementation: Use authenticated-user limits plus request/token/tool-loop caps and proxy-aware network budgets.
controls.verification: Mock model; user limit reaches 429 without provider spend or cross-user blocking.
controls.why: A request or agent loop should not create an unbounded bill.

controls.item: Treat retrieved text and generated output as data
controls.when: LLM input/output, RAG or agent tools
controls.owner: Agent after plan; permission expansion never implicit
controls.implementation: Separate instruction authority from content; validate output and tool arguments outside the prompt.
controls.verification: Local adversarial document cannot cause unauthorized tool effects; log only safe evidence.
controls.why: Retrieved text and model output are not permission to execute actions.

controls.item: Keep retrieval and tool access within each user scope
controls.implementation: Enforce tenant filters and scoped credentials at retrieval/tool boundaries.
controls.verification: Two fake identities cannot retrieve each other’s records or invoke disallowed tools.
controls.why: Tools and retrieval need the same user boundaries as the underlying data.

controls.item: Review skill commands and permission boundaries
controls.when: Agent instructions, scripts and referenced resources
controls.owner: Agent reviews; user approves external actions
controls.implementation: Inventory executable paths, network calls, file scope and untrusted instruction entry points.
controls.verification: Static trace plus later isolated fixture; fetched text cannot authorize commands.
controls.why: Instructions and helper commands should not silently expand their host permissions.

controls.item: Validate MCP authorization and transport boundaries
controls.implementation: Match transport/version; validate token audience, consent and minimal permissions.
controls.verification: Local invalid-audience and unauthorized-tool fixtures fail without external OAuth calls.
controls.why: A token intended for one service should not authorize another.

controls.item: Protect mobile storage and platform entry points
controls.owner: Agent proposes; ask per permissions/auth item
controls.implementation: Select current MASVS/MASTG controls for local storage, links, IPC, permissions and network use.
controls.verification: Use available simulator/device fixtures; unavailable platform tests explicitly NOT RUN.
controls.why: Mobile data and entry points need platform-specific boundaries.

controls.item: Separate desktop content from OS privileges
controls.implementation: Review sandbox/renderer isolation, IPC validation and navigation boundaries.
controls.verification: Local renderer cannot invoke an unapproved privileged operation.
controls.why: Untrusted desktop content should not inherit operating-system privileges.

controls.item: Pin and constrain CI execution
controls.owner: Agent file edits after plan; remote permissions user
controls.implementation: Review full SHA action references, untrusted PR inputs and least token permission.
controls.verification: Static workflow assertions; no real publish/deploy job run.
controls.why: A workflow dependency or pull-request title should not take control of CI.

controls.item: Keep private packages tied to their registry
controls.implementation: Inspect package scope, resolver sources and lockfile integrity without reading tokens.
controls.verification: Offline configuration checks; never publish or probe a collision package.
controls.why: A public package with the same name should not replace a private dependency.

controls.item: Protect package publishing identities
controls.owner: User registry/dashboard; ask per CI identity change
controls.implementation: Use supported 2FA/trusted publisher workflows and minimal credentials.
controls.verification: Review local workflow contract; registry configuration remains unverified until user confirms.
controls.why: Publishing access can change every downstream installation.

controls.item: Trace released artifacts to their source
controls.implementation: Record release provenance and integrity metadata where supported.
controls.verification: Verify local artifact digests/attestations if present; absence is not proof of malware.
controls.why: Traceable artifacts make unexpected changes easier to investigate.

controls.item: Collect and retain only needed personal data
controls.owner: User legal/data decisions; ask per schema item
controls.implementation: Inventory purpose, processors, retention and applicable rights; do not assume consent is always the basis.
controls.verification: Synthetic export/delete checks only after approved data-model scope.
controls.why: Keeping less personal data reduces what must be protected and managed.

controls.item: Plan recovery and watch for failed protections
controls.implementation: Assign incident contact, backup/restore responsibility and useful security-event monitoring.
controls.verification: Approved local restore exercise where available; distinguish plan from tested recovery.
controls.why: A documented response and recovery path helps when something goes wrong.

controls.item: Revisit sources and deeper assurance as the app grows
controls.when: New integrations, data classes or scale
controls.implementation: Refresh source editions and module choices; escalate high-assurance work beyond this skill.
controls.verification: Changed project facts trigger new applicable checks; never re-use old passes as fresh evidence.
controls.why: New features can make an earlier checklist incomplete.

controls.item: Roll out a Content Security Policy
controls.owner: Agent proposes Report-Only; ask separately before enforcement
controls.implementation: Inventory required resource origins; retain existing enforcement and introduce Report-Only only for a new policy. Keep reports local unless data sharing is approved.
controls.verification: A local synthetic violation is observed; expected pages work. Report-Only is never counted as blocked execution.
controls.why: A measured rollout can restrict unwanted scripts without breaking real workflows.

controls.item: Limit public and write-endpoint abuse
controls.when: Sign-up, contact, reset, API-key issuance or public writes
controls.owner: Agent after plan; auth semantics require separate approval
controls.implementation: Set endpoint-specific network/user/API-client budgets, payload limits and timeouts; identify API clients without logging credential values. Preserve legitimate retries and webhooks.
controls.verification: A bounded local sequence reaches 429; a different permitted identity still works and spoofed forwarding headers cannot reset the budget.
controls.why: Public actions can consume resources even without a login.

controls.item: Make automated sign-up and form abuse harder
controls.when: Public sign-up, contact or costly forms
controls.owner: Agent existing local controls after plan; user enables new provider
controls.implementation: Combine endpoint limits with appropriate anti-automation controls. If a challenge provider is chosen, ask before adding the service and validate its result server-side before any side effect.
controls.verification: Mock accepted, rejected, expired and replayed challenge responses; rejected submissions send no email or create no account. No live challenge calls.
controls.why: Forms and sign-up routes should not become spam or resource-amplification tools.

controls.item: Put an appropriate edge proxy in front of public services
controls.owner: User provider/DNS action; ask per infrastructure configuration
controls.implementation: Prefer the hosting platform’s existing TLS/CDN/abuse layer where suitable. Verify origin bypass protection and trusted proxy addresses; do not buy or add another CDN without need and approval.
controls.verification: Local config and topology review; user verifies TLS, origin reachability and protection in provider settings. Local checks cannot prove edge protection.
controls.why: An edge service can handle transport and some abuse before requests reach the app.

controls.item: Keep redirects on approved destinations
controls.when: Return URLs, sign-in redirects or forwarding endpoints
controls.owner: Agent after plan; auth-flow changes ask-first
controls.implementation: Use fixed destination IDs or allowlisted parsed URLs. Reject scheme-relative and encoded bypasses; preserve valid application-relative navigation.
controls.verification: Local benign redirect succeeds; external, //host and encoded attacker destinations cannot become Location targets.
controls.why: A trusted application link should not send someone to an unapproved destination.

controls.item: Authenticate the domain used to send email
controls.when: Application sends email from a custom domain
controls.owner: User DNS and mail provider actions
controls.implementation: Identify actual senders and existing records; propose SPF, provider-issued DKIM and staged DMARC alignment. Never invent DNS values or access signing keys; avoid duplicate SPF records or premature rejection.
controls.verification: User supplies redacted provider verification and a synthetic message’s authentication result. Agent does not change DNS or send email.
controls.why: Receivers need a way to recognize mail sent for your domain.

controls.item: Separate development from production data and credentials
controls.owner: Agent config references after plan; user provisions/rotates
controls.implementation: Use separate environment identifiers and least-privilege credentials; fixtures use synthetic data and mocked services. Do not copy production databases, credentials or environment files.
controls.verification: Inspect variable names and config references; local tests cannot reach production endpoints and use only synthetic records.
controls.why: A local test should never spend production money or change real users’ data.

controls.item: Keep dependency updates arriving automatically
controls.owner: Agent config after plan; user enables remote features
controls.implementation: Configure the detected ecosystem’s supported update service and review cadence. Preserve lockfile boundaries and script policy; do not auto-merge major or untested changes.
controls.verification: Parse update config and check paths against manifests; local patch/minor updates pass relevant checks. Scheduling remotely stays unverified.
controls.why: Regular small updates reduce avoidable dependency drift.
